STATIC LEARNING EDITION · developing

Sensitive dependence on initial conditions

Two nearly identical beginnings can become visibly different. The word “can” needs careful quantifiers.

Open interactive route Exact archive record

Manipulation

Run paired logistic trajectories and change the feedback parameter. Keep the initial separation and stopping time explicit.

Pattern

Different parameters can change the observed separation pattern. A finite pair explores particular states, not every neighborhood.

Mechanism

The archive’s definition requires a uniform positive threshold, every base point and radius, and some nearby witness and time. Binary64 rounding can also affect numerical trajectories.

Vocabulary

sensitive dependence
The particular quantified metric property quoted below.
metric
The declared way of measuring distance.

Notation

d(x, y)
Distance between two states in the chosen metric.
Tⁿ(x)
Apply the map T n times to x.

Formal statement

Context: metric dynamical systems

T has sensitive dependence on initial conditions iff there exists δ>0 such that for every x in X and every ε>0 there exist y in X and n>=0 with d(x,y)<ε and d(T^n(x),T^n(y))>δ.

Sensitivity alone is not a universal definition of chaos.

    verify · classification

    Which quantifier is doing the work?

    Match each role in the archive’s metric definition of sensitivity.

    1. A positive separation threshold δ, chosen once for the system.
    2. A base point x and a positive neighborhood radius ε.
    3. A nearby point y and a time n, allowed to depend on x and ε.
    Hint

    The order is: exists δ; for every x and ε; exists y and n.

    Answer and its scope
    A positive separation threshold δ, chosen once for the system. → There exists
A base point x and a positive neighborhood radius ε. → For every
A nearby point y and a time n, allowed to depend on x and ε. → There exists

    The quantifier order is essential. One impressive-looking trajectory cannot discharge it.
